Today we are beginning our beta trail of Vulkan! Vulkan is a modern graphics technology that will help RuneScape communicate with your computer's graphics hardware. You can think of it as the bridge between the game engine and your GPU, telling your device how to draw everything you see on screen. You can access the Vulkan open beta build of RuneScape via the Graphics Mode setting in the startup options menu: just switch it to 'Vulkan', check out the news post for more information.

Good people of Gielinor, thank you for coming.

For those of you who do not know me, my name is Seren.
Some call me the goddess of the elves.
I have called you here because you represent every race of people and every god on Gielinor.

There is a threat, a threat which faces every one of us.
One you may be unaware of.

They are beings, older than our world.
Indeed, they created this world, and indirectly everything on it.

Great artefacts, like the Stone of Jas, which have brought us
war and woe for millennia, are merely their discarded tools.

They are so powerful, so far beyond all of us,
that even we gods are nothing more than ants to them.

For the entire lifetime of this planet they have slept,
but now they are waking up.
To them, this planet and all of its people are nothing more than food for their children.

They laid their eggs in the heart of the planet, and when they hatch,
they will consume Gielinor and all life on it.

Then they will move on to the rest of the universe, destroying world after world,
until their work is finished and there is nothing but darkness.
Because I too am their child.

It fills my heart with pride to be considered the goddess of my people,
but that is not my true identity.

My mother was an elder god. Though weak, deformed, abandoned.
No Threat to Gielinor.
She created me, millions of years ago, along with- with... another.

I went out into the universe, discovered mortal life, and though it took time,
I learned to appreciate the joy and wonder that your kind brings to existence.
I do not share the goal of my kin. I would not see life on this planet, in this universe, ended.
We have only one chance to avoid this fate.

You must meet with the elder gods.
You must go before them, prove to them that you are more than merely food to be consumed.
I am sure that they will come to see your value as I have.

That is why I have brought you here. To warn you.
To plead with you to make this case.

It is only by working together that you can do this.
Only united can you show the elder gods that you are worthy.

The world guardian arrived just too late.
Kerapac's plan had worked flawlessly.
With a triumphant shout he plunged the staff into the Needle to absorb its power.
Gail watched in horror as control of the Needle was torn from her and given to the dragonkin.

In an instant, she was Gail no more.
Primrose stood, staring at the monster before her.
Kerapac roared in triumph, the power of the Needle now his to command.
He took to the air, and the Needle vanished from sight at the whim of its new master.
He flew east to the coast and out across the sea, vanishing into a great storm.
And there he set to work on the next stage of his endeavour...

What an unusual find! This strange device plays back recorded sound from things call 'song eggs'. The audio is emitted from stylised baby birds sat in a nest.
This multi-coloured coat is very vibrant and distinctive. It perhaps suggests a connection between the aviansie and colourful mating displays by many types of bird.
This weapon is not unlike other lances our archaeologists have discovered, but attached to it is a device akin to a cannon barrel. At best this would provide a single shot.
Perhaps made to mimic certain bird plumage, this flamboyant headgear certainly attracts attention.
Research teams have pored over Howl's notes and believe this so-called chuluu stone's uses were as wide-ranging as an ingredient in alchemy spells and in producing healing potions.
Perhaps less fashionable than other artefacts discovered at Stormguard, but perhaps more practical, especially if worn while flying around in the strong winds here.
Golem technology is a process mostly lost to those of us in the current age. It appears golem production was at its height during the Third Age, and at Stormguard Citadel especially so.
The instructions discovered with (or still being used by) golems that survive to the current day tend to be paper based. This device seems mechanical in nature. How strange.
Music appears to have been very popular with the aviansie, even given what the site this was discovered at was used for.
This odd stringed instrument produces a very distinct and pleasing sound. The head of it appears to depict some sort of animal, though it's unclear as to which.
At first glance, this device appears like a regular spyglass, but multiple pieces of coloured glass can be bent in front of the lens letting the user see things the naked eye cannot.
Aviansie do not typically have need to wear goggles while flying, according to site manager Gee'ka, but these goggles allow anyone to have superior vision in low light and even in the dark.
Fashion is abundant at Stormguard, which is odd given its purpose, but even inventors need to relax. Given how windy it is there, this parasol was likely more for show than function.
Gerege is an aviansie word much like 'pass'. These small metal ingots were used to communicate a person's rank or station, and could be used to gain access to secure areas.
Where the Ikovian gerege allowed us access to Stormguard Citadel itself, this Stormguard gerege may allow us passage into the site's more sensitive and secure areas.
It appears Howl attempted to make various weapons from aetherium, before settling on the godsword. Though aetherium is light, perhaps it was not suitable to make a decent bow.
Aetherium alloy also works as a conduit for magical energies, so this godstaff seems a better approach than a bow, but presumably the more direct connection of a sword was more effective.
Here it is - a prototype version of the now legendary godsword. This weapon was constructed by the advanced alloy known as aetherium, smithed by the aviansie inventor Howl himself.
The team are unsure entirely what the purpose of this device was, but it seems to have a reaction to the gravitational core holding the destroyed remnants of Stormguard together.
Quintessence, according to some of Howl's notes found by our teams, was very hard to come by, hence the invention of this device to help track it down.
While an upgrade for the wingsuit, to provide some combat utility, we've advised against our archaeologists from applying them to their own wingsuits until we know more.
The Dayguard were one of the two tribes that helped to protect Stormguard from a direct assault (though there is no evidence that such an assault was ever made).
The Nightguard comprised of aviansie with better night vision and stealth capabilities. They were Stormguard's primary raiding force.
This device share some similarities with another device found at Stormguard, though seems to be more for recording sounds than playing them back, and in a much small form.
This three-dimensional astrolabe is a map of the heavens. Considering other artefacts discovered at Stormguard, this was likely used to keep track of various cosmic occurrences.
A children's carved wooden toy in the shape of some sort of glider, but with some bird-like stylings to it also.
This children's toy appears to depict an Armadylean golem, according to Gee'ka, but its proportions suggest a much larger variant than any she has seen before.
This helm is fashioned to look like an enraged beast of some kind, and is made with natural materials.
From what our consultant, Zanik, has imparted, the Dorgeshuun tribe splintered from Bandos in mid-Third Age. That spears of their tribal design are still found at the Warforge is curious...
These vicious swords have a hooked end, presumably for pulling enemies closer or sweeping shields out of the way, to open victims up to a follow up attack.

How strange! This oversized mask appears to be poking fun at the god Armadyl. Worn by goblins in the arena no doubt to amuse Bandos. Researchers are looking to see if any other gods were ridiculed by these big head masks.
We are unsure if this anchor was a wielded weapon or simply used in the typical way. Staining around the walls of the Crucible suggest it may have been purposefully flooded for special events.
A ritual sceptre would have been the primary use for this crozier, but it could have also substituted as a magic wand of sorts.
This mitre would have been worn by a particularly devout follower of Bandos, or the Big High War God as site manager Zanik informs us he was also known as.
While more of a ritual item, this orb, with a small Kyzaj symbol atop it, could have been used to channel magic spells.
A rather simple sword, that seems best suited for skewering opponents.
Zanik tells us the Horogothgar were infamous for eating their defeated enemies, including other goblins. Tellingly, the inside of this pot still holds an unpleasant lingering smell to it.
Parts of this crown appear to share iconography with artefacts discovered at one of our other digs. This headgear was likely worn by a goblin tribe sold to the god Zamorak.
Given where these were found, the team can only speculate that these rings were placed over the horn of a nosorog. They come in different sizes and colours that seem to stack in a pleasing pattern.
The Kal-i-kra, our site manager informs us, was a tribe of beings from which Bandos originated. This crown would have been worn by the tribe's chieftain.
Every side of this weapon has a different implement - a spike on top, a flat hammer surface, a bladed edge, a pick-like head and a 'tenderiser'. The team have dubbed it the 'switch army mace'.
A nosorog appears to have been the original owner of this warhorn, which would have been used in the heat of battle for commanders to communicate orders to their soldiers.
A heavy rubber ball covered in spikes suggests the 'game' that was played with it was a dangerous one.
Considering the size, this hand axe-like weapon (that was styled after Bandos's 'Kyzaj' symbol) was likely wielded by larger creatures such as ogres.
This sword, while seemingly crude with its notched edge, is actually finely crafted and balanced. The bronze it is made from seems impressively strong, even when compared to iron or steel.

The name of this weapon loosely translates as 'mega hitter', or so our cave goblin researchers tell us. You wouldn't think glass fragments sandwiched between two wooden boards would be so deadly, but put it in an ourg's hands...
This strange contraption seems nothing more than a framework for chaining up to four goblins together. The metal bars are rigid and sharpened.
Considering most goblin headgear is constructed from reclaimed materials, these well-constructed and decorative crowns stand out. They sport a design reminiscent of Saradominist symbology.
A hand-sculpted icon of Bandos, made with clay. The work is unrefined, but the end result is remarkably accurate to descriptions of the god Bandos.
The Kyzaj shape of this crude clay sculpture is evident. It looks to be the same size as a recess in the back of the throne sat looking over the Crucible...

Nosorog are seemingly large, bulky quadrupeds with a giant horn on their snout. Research suggests these animals were brought here from another world, for goblins to survive against in the Crucible arena.
Each goblin tribe has its own symbol, rituals and customs. This Thorobshuun battle standard perhaps suggests this tribe was particularly martial.
The team are not clear if this was a standard size shield (proportionally, for an ourg) or an oversized shield for goblins to cower behind. Considering Bandos, it was probably both.

What a strange contraption! Remnants of malachite and traces of water were found in two brittle clay chambers. It appears this was a thrown weapon that would shatter on impact and create a toxic cloud.

The fully restored legendary Spear of Annihilation. Speculation is rife at the Archaeology Guild that this might be the weapon Bandos used to ascend to godhood; however, there is no good evidence to support this.

On closer inspection, this is clearly just a replica of a centurion's dress sword, used for training prospective guild members. It makes sense to not entrust fragile, age-old artefacts to inexperienced hands. Still, it's a very good replica.

The origins of this artefact are unclear, but it appears to incorporate elements from the four main factions that fought in the God Wars. There also appears to be trace elements of a fifth faction, which brings into question the 'tetra' naming.
These containers were primarily used to store goods for transport, both liquids and solids. Wine was the most common good stored within them.
This ostentatious ornament appears to wrap around a unicorn's horn. It is very beautifully crafted and adorned with small gemstones.

This ceremonial saddle suggests that unicorns were at least sometimes ridden. It seems unlikely that the icyene would use them as mounts, nor centaurs or lions, so it remains a mystery as to who might have done so.
That this vase remained decently intact enough to be restored is testament to the craftsmanship that went into it. It was likely hand-made in Everlight's oikoi studios, from the local keramos clay.

This strange device, at least partly clockwork, has no immediately obvious mechanical use. It has stumped our researchers. It is, however, incredibly intricate and well beyond what was thought possible at the time.
This bizarre and intricate device is something of a mystery. Study suggests that it might be clockwork in construction, but what purpose it may have served is lost on us.

While javelins such as this may have proved somewhat effective in martial combat, their primary use appears to have been in certain Dominion Games events. Likely they were used to showcase accuracy over long distances.
This bronze medal appears to have been awarded to third place participants of the Dominion Games. These metal choices seem to be the source of our own more modern competitive sporting events.
This silver medal appears to have been awarded to second place participants of the Dominion Games. These metal choices seem to be the source of our own more modern competitive sporting events.
These wicker pelte shields appear to have been used in sparring, perhaps during certain Dominion Games events. It would have been completely ineffective in actual combat.
This artefact appears to be a variant of the more commonly hallowed lanterns, and channelled the magic of Everlight into an ever-living flame. It was presumably used as part of the Dominion Games.
This stringed instrument, also known as a lyre, has turtle shell as part of its construction. Sea turtles have been spotted swimming off the coast by our archaeologists.
While this instrument has a very simple construction, is is beautifully crafted and still carries a pleasing note.
The more intricate of the instruments found at Everlight, this violin would have taken a lot of practice to master.
This artefact suggests that icyene of old ate fish, which makes sense being they lived on the coast.
This stylised idol of a female icyene has its arms folded, presumably in some sort of reverential pose to the god Saradomin.
This stylised idol of a male icyene has its arms folded, presumably in some sort of reverential pose to the god Saradomin.
What these artefacts were actually named or used for is not something we've been able to discover so far, beyond their use in funerary practices. Vanescula came up with the term 'frying pan'.

These lanterns could purportedly carry a spark of Everlight's magical power within them, providing a constant source of light. Unfortunately, we have had to substitute a simple candle in place of the magic.
Evidence suggests these bowls were primarily used for cleaning activities such as the washing of hands and wings. Residues suggest the water within them was scented with flower petals.
The design of this cup is striking and distinctive and, though faded, depicts a scene on its side. The image on this cup looks to depict the light atop the main structure at Everlight.
Researchers wonder what use the icyene could have had for a dagger, considering they could fly and strike from a distance. Perhaps it was more of a tool than a weapon.

The lance appears to be far less common a weapon for the icyene that the spear, likely because it would have required more specialised training to wield effectively, but also many of the examples we have found are on the ornate side.
The spear was the primary armament of standard icyene troops, giving them both versatility and range, making great use of their ability to fly.

Short swords such as this would primarily have been wielded by the hetairoi, icyene knights from noble families. While effective, they were a less dependable weapon for more martial forces, not taking advantage of the icyene's ability to fly.
This painting appears to depict a much-loved Dominion Games medallist, but the scene itself is quite melancholy, perhaps in an attempt to convey humility or hubris. It's hard to tell.
This painting seems to depict an aerial view of Everlight, showing the landmass more clearly than we can make out beneath the surface of the water now.
Here is a painting that depicts the god Saradomin in a particularly flattering image. The halo, or 'glory', behind his head denotes his divine stature.

Asclepius appears to be a figure from early icyene culture, according to research. There is some connection with him being a renowned healer or surgeon. This rod - a snake or worm twisted around a spindle - is also connected with medicine.
Translations of this scroll mark it out as a series of steps to achieve 'enlightenment'. Saradomin is namechecked frequently, but other words stand out, such as nectar and ambrosia.
Markings on this stone tablet depict some fundamentals of mathematics, in particular geometry, algebra and references to something called the 'golden ratio'.
The design of this branding iron seems both familiar and not. Despite where this was discovered, it appears to have been used to mark cult members, so they could identify each other in public.
Researchers have so far been unable to determine what the style of this metallic design is supposed to depict, but functionally it acts as a dampener for chaotic energies.
This is a highly unusual find, suggesting Star Lodge hides sinister secrets. The eye-like design of this crest is very unnerving.
Members of the Order of Dis supposedly wore these masks during sacrificial rituals and other cult duties, to hide their identities. This lesser demon mask would likely have been for acolytes.
Members of the Order of Dis supposedly wore these masks during sacrificial rituals and other cult duties, to hide their identities. This imp mask would likely have been for neophytes.
Members of the Order of Dis supposedly wore these masks during sacrificial rituals and other cult duties, to hide their identities. This greater demon mask would likely have been for hyeraphs.
Haladies are unwieldy weapons without significant strength behind them. This example has three blades pointing in different directions, giving lots of offensive and defensive options.
Sometimes colloquially referred to as a 'punching dagger', demon warriors would have worn these in pairs and put their considerable strength behind each stabbing punch.
While it may look more like a tool, the zaghnal was effectively a pickaxe design refined into an effective armour-piercing weapon, though is technically classified as a warhammer.
Hookah pipes were often used in communal smoking dens, where groups of revellers could smoke flavoured tobaccos. The design of this pipe is almost hypnotic.
There is little to say about these manacles other than to comment on where they were discovered, that being in the Dungeon of Disorder's 'guest quarters'.
Found in Star Lodge, this wine goblet is certainly extravagant. It is suggestive of the wealth of the clientele that the lodge saw fit to entertain.
The Order of Dis cult we've discovered were the seedy underbelly of Star Lodge. It is unknown whether the 'Dis robes' word play was intentionally knowing or just an unfortunate coincidence.
It is hard to know what this abstract painting is trying to depict. Black is the most abundant colour, but there is vibrancy on display, and while chaotic in style, patterns also emerge.
This painting is title the Lake of Fire, suggesting this may be an abstract image of lava. Is this a depiction of the Source or somewhere else?
Movario informs us that Pandemonium is an alternate name for the Infernal Realms, the home of demonkind. The tapestry named for it is quite striking.
This wickedly snaking blade was most likely used for ritual sacrifices, likely upon the altar within the Dungeon of Disorder.

While abstract, the research consensus is that this metallic sculpture represents two intertwined lovers. This was likely an ornament on display within Star Lodge, perhaps suggesting something about the lodge.
The theme of this metal sculpture appears to be either control or possession. One figure seems to be manipulating the other.
This abstract metal sculpture evokes two figures, one seemingly tormenting the other. It's very unnerving, yet still pleasingly aesthetic.
While the team have dubbed this a dog collar, it's clearly for a very large dog. Considering where it was found, the research team has suggested it was for a hellhound.
This trident-like tool, made from this area's hellfire metal, has been nicknamed the 'devil fork'. Perhaps demons used it to herd prisoners about the Source.
There are lots of trophies found at the Source, though this one was likely not on display in Star Lodge proper, given how alien and strange it looks.
Whoever collected trophies here clearly travelled far and wide to have bagged a larupia, given they are primarily found in the area now known as the Feldip Hills.
Lions were understood to have been introduced to Gielinor by Saradomin, or at least most frequently fought alongside the icyene.
Why specifically a she-wolf was hunted is lost on the research team, however the trophies found where this one was come across as some sort of subtle warning.
Another trophy not for public display. Virii, also sometimes known as blood reavers, are the chthonian equivalent of hellhounds.
Tsutsaroth demons typically wear very little armour, and don't really need to make their visage more fearsome.
Demons are not particularly well known for wearing armour, so why they would choose to protect their shoulders specifically is both odd and unknown.
There is much speculation as to where this piercing may have been placed by the tsutsaroth that wore it. Perhaps it was a mark of rank or achievement?
Urumi are an archaic type of whip, this one constructed from razor-thin hellfire metal. They were as dangerous to the wielder as any target. A weapon of terror.
Even as early as the Second Age, inhabitants of Gielinor knew it was a spheroid planet rather than a flat dimensional plane. The Zarosian Empire placed a strong emphasis on educating its citizens.
Whatever wordings or symbols once resided on this magical tablet have long since eroded, making its magic inert. There's now no telling what effect this tablet might have had.
An early form of watch, more akin to a portable sundial. Something like this would still have been quite effective and accurate.
These plans seem to capture the moment in time that led up the battle that caused Kharid-et to fall. It's likely this plan was concocted by the praetorians stationed here at the time.
Even members of the Zarosian clergy carried weapons, though it seems this mace was primarily for ceremonial uses.
This censer was likely used in various religious ceremonies to scent the air. Residue within might suggest they occasionally carried hallucinogenic compounds.

This crozier is an example of what leaders within the Zarosian priesthood would have carried to show their rank within the church. This one is a relatively mundane example, no doubt from a lowlier member of the church.
Mitres such as this would likely only have been worn by those highest in the Zarosian papacy, most notably the Pontifex Maximus, though how they fit them over the antennae is unclear.

A sculpture of Zamorak. Most samples we find of these are smashed beyond our ability to restore them. Presumably, the inhabitants had more pressing matters than desecrating such idols, and also little time to do so.
These pendants were carried by certain ranking members of the Zarosian military, as well as the custodians of this fort's carcerem. They effectively acted as passes into areas of high security.

The standard arms of a Zarosian legionary. While only a short sword, at the time it was the superior metal in comparison to other armies, and likely proved effective in combination with the standard shield.
The standard defensive attire of an imperial legionary, the rank of file of the Zarosian military. Research suggests a cohort would lock shields in various formations when facing opposing armies.

This book - the Orconomicom, aka the Book of Orcus - was used as a magical focus primarily by praetorian guards, but seemingly some of Kharid-et's pontifex also owned copies. It primarily focuses on necromancy.

This painting appears to depict the primary meeting between Zaros and the Mahjarrat. This would have been a pivotal moment in the Zarosian-Kharidian War, something inhabitants of this fort likely partook in.
This painting appears to depict a battle between Zaros himself and Tumeken, the leader of the Menaphite pantheon. The title roughly translate to 'Shadow of the Sun'.

This painting of the First Legion upon arrival on Gielinor, depicted here locked into combat with the divine hydra, Loarnab. Early evidence suggests this first legion was commanded by Duke Nemesis the Inescapable, a demon from Infernus.
Dr Nabanik has identified this figure as a Mahjarrat called Azzanadra, the presumed leader of the Church of Zaros. The strange antennae on the head are found on many pontifex robes.
These signet rings were used only by high-ranking members of the Church of Zaros, in order to access secure areas of the fort.

Our research suggests the praetorians carried these as weapons, each containing a demon soul. Once thrown at a group of enemies, the demon would steal a host and set upon the rest. The slang term for them was 'diabolus'.
The hood of a set of praetorian robes. It's very heavy and well armoured, which is unusual for most modern magic users. They include a covering for the face, presumably for the sake of anonymity.
While doubling up as religious robing, this gear's primary uses was as heavy protection for praetorians - warrior mages of the Zarosian Secret Police. It suggests their work was dangerous.

The standard praetorian staff appears to include a small censer, though for what reason is currently not known. We have made some finds that suggest a more ornate and powerful version of this magical staff existed.

The term 'primis elementis' roughly translates to 'primordial elements'. We believe these totems were carried by each legion or cohort as a battle standard, and the loss of one was a source of great shame for a legion.
The remaining legible text on this scroll suggests the spell written upon it was necromantic in nature.
This grisly little spell appears to steal the life force of an enemy and transfer it back to the caster.
From what we can make out, this spell's use appears to have been to freeze its target in place and/or cause them to rout.
While incomplete, we can tell this scroll would have caused a cloud of thick smoke to be conjured, though the smoke's effect is unknown.
Venators acted as scouts, hunters and spies for the Zarosian Army, so travelled light, hence why they carried these daggers as standard issue arms.
The venator light crossbow was built for fast reloading to couple with the hit-and-run tactics that Zarosian scouts seemingly employed.
These glass vials appear to simply be an earlier form of potion container, though there isn't enough trace of whatever it once may have contained to identify it.
Finally, we have discovered an icon of the Empty Lord himself. No such icons have been discovered at the Varrock Dig Site, so we are lucky with how well preserved Kharid-et is.
Ewers such as this were primarily used to store water making them incredibly valuable at this fort. This area was not desert at the time in which it operated, but was likely incredibly humid.
This tankard has a built-in lid, likely in order to keep the contents from contamination by insects and particulates. Some of those we've found contain trace elements of alcoholic beverages.

This dummy, likely used to drill legionaries within the castra, are fashioned after what appear to be chthonian demons. Being the chthonians were also citizens of the Zarosian Empire, this styling comes across as an odd choice.

The monolith has given me information on the icyene structure known as Everlight,
a lighthouse on Morytania's east coast.

More than just a lighthouse, though,
it served as a beacon of hope for the icyene race, newly migrated to Gielinor.

But what could power such a beacon, to shine
so brightly day and night across the surrounding 'Hallowed' lands?

And what opposing force of darkness could have snuffed out the Everlight
and sunk it beneath the waves?
The sacking of Everlight was an atrocity, to be sure, but it was just a place, a thing.
The loss of not only many icyene people, but also their way of life, was the true tragedy here.

Lord Drakan and his vampyres took such offence at this beacon
that they could not abide its existence.

Yet the surviving icyene, to this day, carry Everlight's
warmth and hope within them, an example to us all.
Everlight - Dominion Games stadium excavation site
Lions and Unicorns and Centaurs, Oh My!
Many mounds of earth sit upon Everlight's central island.
Everlight's central island is covered with burial mounds - icyene mass graves for those who fell during the sacking of Everlight at the hands of Lord Drakan.
The amphitheatre stage is now sunk beneath the waves.
Whatever epics were performed at Everlight's amphitheatre have been lost to time. Unfortunately, the team could not find any more detailed information about this area.
The remains of an oval stadium are evident at Everlight.
The icyene instigated the Dominion Games - a huge sporting tournament for them and their allies. We've found evidence that lions, unicorns, centaurs, humans, aviansie and even seasingers took part!
Everlight's Oikos island is littered with homes and studios.
Artisan icyene worked and lived in the Oikos area of Everlight, using local resources to craft various containers and ceremonial items.
A ruined temple sits upon a high point of the southern area of Everlight.
The acropolis on Everlight was home to icyene academics, philosophers and poets. They would have gathered here for public readings, talks and presentations, as well as debates.
Some remains of icyene soldiers in the underwater cave are in a line.
It appears a squad of optimatoi made a last stand in front of Everlight's entrance.
Evidence of ancient clockwork machinery has been discovered at Everlight.
The mechanism in Everlight's foundations appears to power an elevator that carries people up and down the length of the lighthouse. If we could get this working, we could reach the top!

I struggle to understand the monolith's directions to the 'Source'.
It points north-west, but the distance and depth are unclear, variable.

At least Movario seems confident we are digging in the right place. He explores
rumours of a cult that seemingly operated in this area throughout the Third Age.

Though what the Source itself actually is remains a mystery.
Perhaps all of this is due to the chaotic nature of the thing?

The monolith revealed this chaotic nature to me.
That is why it is so interested in learning more about the Source...

Movario was right! The buried Star Lodge contained a secret
cult dungeon hidden beneath it, and within that a portal to the Source itself!

How many were taken by this cult and sacrificed over the centuries?
It's horrific to even think about.

To have your soul ripped out to power a portal to Dis,
to bring forth demons into this world!

Dagon the Gatekeeper, an unwitting and unwilling participant in this hellscape,
is as much a victim as those sacrificed. Is Dagon what the monolith desired we uncover?

This building upon which the Jolly Boar Inn was built appears to be a lodge of some sort.
Paperwork found onsite suggests this place was named Star Lodge. Records show it was buried by the Forinthry explosion, and the Jolly Boar built atop it in a subsequent age.
A secret cult was in hiding beneath the lodge. This place is creepy.

Symbology found in the dungeon matches that of a rumoured cult known as the Order of Dis, previously only thought to be a myth. It seems these followers of Zamorak hid in plain sight under the auspices of Saradomin and kept their presence secret for an age!
We're unsure where the portal has led, but we've made a significant discovery! Navigating this chaotic space is, however, proving tricky for our dig teams.

Research places the Infernal Source directly beneath the Wilderness Crater! To think this place was here, abandoned, all this time. The research team have reported on a very vocal imp being found in this area and suggest you investigate...
As the team delves deeper into the Infernal Source, the landscape is becoming more alien and unwelcoming, for example a sculpture made from hellhound skulls.

That demonic remains even exist in this space in fossilised form suggests this space may cross over with infernal space in some way. One of the hellhound skulls had a dog collar placed around its neck, sporting the name 'Duke'.
The source of the screaming seems to be a demonic entity trapped at the bottom of this space. None of our archaeologists dare to venture that far down.

What we can see from the level above is that the demon below is trapped somehow. It is also surrounded by a twelve-headed circular statue, but we are not quite sure what any of it means at this point. We need to get closer, but the portal is too chaotic - we need to figure out how to make it work.
Upon closer inspection, the twelve-headed circular statue matches descriptions of an ages-old entity, an incredibly large specimen of a hydra.

Wow! What a find! Researchers have found the hydra gate was at one point a living creature! The petrified remains appear to match descriptions of an ancient deity named Loarnab. It still hums with a small amount of residual energy.
This is a book containing a transcription of Trindine's memory.

The Zarosian Empire's very existence was once the greatest of archaeological
mysteries for us to uncover, and we achieved that here at Senntisten.

And although the empire was supposedly sprawling, it was so utterly destroyed
that finding a near intact fort buried beneath the sands is cause for celebration!

The monolith has a strong connection with something buried deep beneath this
fort, however. Was the monolith itself Zarosian? No, surely not; it's beyond ancient.

There is only one way to find out what the connection is.
We must dig deep at Kharid-et and discover what lies beneath...

Kharid-et was truly forsaken. Though it fell right at the beginning of the Third Age,
it has remained untouched for millenia.

The place is filled with the ghosts of its past.
It's a wonder none of the archaeologists have encountered them so far.

It is clear to us now why the monolith wished for us to dig here.
The magical readings are off the charts!

I feel we have only scratched the surface of what
ancient magical power sits beneath here, buried in the shadows...
The wall we are using to enter Kharid-et was seemingly breached from the outside long ago.
Research suggests Kharid-et was under siege by an army of demons loyal to Zamorak, very early on in the Third Age. The protective shield that sometimes activates here must have been breached.
The castra, which roughly translates to 'camp', was primarily where the rank and file soldiers resided in the fort.
This area of Kharid-et was mostly used as a training ground, as well as housing for legionaries, though some buildings appear to have been reserved for imperial officers.
The carcerem, which translates to 'prison', was an area of the fort used to temporarily hold lawbreakers.
The team suggest that the various magical Legatus and Pontifex barriers could be passed through if you hold or wear the correct artefact...but they aren't sure which artefacts.
The sanctum, or chapel, is primarily where members of the Zarosian Church went for worship.

This particular sanctum appears to have paid fealty to a demon named Orcus - one of the empire's chthonian dukes, according to Dr Nabanik - who was supposedly known for its necromantic ability. Orcus's inverted pentagram symbology is abundant.
The culinarum, or kitchens, are pretty standard fare for a fort of this size.

There's not a huge deal of interest to be found in the kitchens, save for a strange device on one of the walls there. This kitchen could have served food to an entire legion - over a thousand troops and support staff!
How unusual - an entire building hidden away in an overlapping realm!

The praetorium has somehow been shifted into the Shadow Realm in order to hide its existence! It took the shield pylon effect and another shadow delving ability to even see the war table, which suggests multiple levels of shadow. Perhaps there is something else even deeper?
There is a hidden vault beneath Kharid-et! What wonders might it hold?

Research suggests other, smaller vaults may still be hidden here, but the one we've discovered was clearly of great importance to be hidden how it was. The team wonders what it might contain within...

This seal contains innate magic allowing wielders to pass through Kharid-et's protective barrier. It would have been used by the fort's soldiers and scouting parties to quickly and easily return into the safety of the fort.

The aviansie's use of floating citadels is already well known now,
thanks to the resurgence of their use as clan citadels.

Yet Stormguard, it seems, was an incredibly
well-kept secret for it to be rediscovered only now, many ages on.

What secrets has it held for all this time, floating above our very heads?
What wonders might it hold?

The monolith has no further information to share here.
Stormguard is a mystery even to it...and it wants to learn.

Stormguard was Armadyl's secret research, development and
weapons testing facility, within which the Godsword was forged.

Its presence shrouded in secrecy, along with a cloaking storm cloud,
and forever moving across the skies to protect its existence.

Its many secrets lost to time, as the citadel was
sundered by the Forinthry explosion and its remnants set adrift.

Yet now, a chance to recover the ahead-of-their-time designs
of the aviansie alchemist and inventor 'Howl'.

Little is known about the Temple of Ikov, given how little of it still stands in the current age.
The research team has uncovered that the Ikovians were early human followers of Armadyl, and that the temple stands as a memorial to some sort of massacre of the Ikovians in the early Third Age.
Stormguard's landing pad is littered with megaliths. We're not sure yet of their significance, but they are reminiscent of other cultures' so-called 'deer stones'.

Aviansie typically fight along with a partner - a spouse or close friend. If one of a coupling dies, the survivor typically joins the keshik Dayguard or Nightguard and it becomes their new family. These memorial stones remember their lost partners.

This area of Stormguard is littered with remnants of destroyed golems, most notable of which is the arm of a giant war golem. There's also a wealth of strange and wonderful devices and advanced weaponry.
The Stormguard Citadel appears to have been some sort of secret testing facility, not solely for weapons, but no doubt that during the God Wars weapon development was a primary concern.
The outer parts of what remains of Stormguard seems to contain the ruins of old guard towers.

The Dayguard and Nightguard keshik warriors were seemingly stationed at Stormguard in part to protect its more scientific inhabitants, should the external lightning cloud shielding fail, but also to test out various experimental weapons.
An alchemical laboratory sits floating higher than other remaining sections of Stormguard, filled with all kinds of arcane and mystical devices we don't understand.

According to various blueprints and notebooks, this laboratory was home to an aviansie alchemist who went by the codename 'Howl' (likely to protect his true identity). His works are far ahead of other technology we have dug up from the Third Age, and his ideas well ahead of their time.
A drafting table sits within Stormguard's workshop, upon which sit many blueprints, notes and books all written in an unusual cipher.
The research team have cracked Howl's cipher! We can now understand this eccentric alchemist's designs and start trying to build some of them...

This set of artificial wings was originally created as a prosphetic for injured aviansie, but work just as well at giving flight to the flightless, albeit only nearby Stormguard Citadel's gravitational core.

The monolith shared what it could about the Warforge,
but it's as you would expect from a Bandosian construction.

Bandos's mercenary armies are quite well documented in comparison to
other Third Age events, after all, and they had to be trained somewhere.

What strikes me most, however, is that the few artefacts discovered so far
are not consistent with other Bandosian creations.

Who or what created the armaments for Bandos's mercenaries,
and why is this secret so well buried?

Bandos's capriciousness and cruelty knew no bounds.
Prior to his eviction, he buried his goblin charges beneath the dirt.

Left them to splinter and fight, trapped in darkness - the Forge Wars - and to
devolve into beings bent only on fighting for survival.

The abducted Imcando dwarf, Thalmund, once the flaming heart
of the Warforge, was their only saviour.

All goblins revered him for his fine weaponsmithing, and
so was he able to eventually dig an escape tunnel and lead them back to the surface.
Warforge - South goblin tunnels excavation site
The underground arena we've uncovered is still in a quite well-preserved condition.

Only goblin remains have been discovered within the Warforge's Crucible arena. Other artefacts suggest this arena was used to teach goblin warfare, but clearly, it wasn't exactly safe, and only the fittest goblins survived.
There are a series of barricaded chambers south of the luminescent underground river, with lots of scattered weapons.

The research team suspects the chambers in the south of the Warforge consist of sleeping areas - a cramped dormitory for most of the goblins that lived here, a 'luxury' boudoir for the current tournament champion, and a series of pens for various animals and their keepers.
The chambers in the northern part of these goblin tunnels are littered with barricades and signs of a skirmish.

The chambers north of the river consist of an armoury, a sparring area and a ritual area/shrine to the 'Big High War God', whom we know to be Bandos. There is evidence that there was a great deal of fighting in these tunnels.
The source of heat from beneath the Crucible turns out to be a dwarven forge. What is a dwarven forge doing hidden within a Bandosian stronghold?

The research team has discovered that the forge beneath the Crucible is of Imcando construction! Evidence points to a kidnapped Imcando dwarf being taken as a prisoner and forced to smith weapons for the Warforge, among other things.
Archaeologists have uncovered a hidden area behind Bandos's throne, containing a variety of weapons.

It seems that Bandos left this place in something of a hurry, being that he left behind a number of Kal-i-kra artefacts. Our researchers suggest the Kal-i-kra were a tribe from which Bandos originated before his ascension. Some rare finds here, indeed!
The mechanism that was discovered in the side of Bandos's throne likely unlocks something nearby. Perhaps the research team can figure out how it works.
The research team believe that placing a 'Forged in War' Kyzaj sculpture into the recess on the side of Bandos's throne will unlock something nearby...

I was there, in the year of Croesus. The year the fungus killed fifty thousand people, and the Tenth Legion were annihilated.
It was the Second Age, not long after the end of the Kharidian Campaign.
An expedition returned from the Unquiet Ocean with a very unusual species of fungus.
The fools thought they could turn it into a weapon. A botanical plague they could unleash on the enemies of the Empire.
They called it Croesus. Its spores infested the bodies of the dead, spreading and growing.
They fed it slaves, tested it, burned away weakness, forced it to evolve. They did their jobs far too well.
After one serious breach, they were ordered to cease their work. They didn't.
Inevitably, Croesus broke free into the city again, choking the streets with its putrescent growth.
Nothing could stop it. Priests and guards alike were powerless, and their bodies only served to fuel its flourishing.
I was with the Tenth Legion when we were recalled from the border to combat the infestation.
After days of fighting, my wings ached and my dragonfire was spent.
We razed miles of city to contain it. The Legion were almost completely wiped out. It still wasn't enough.
In the end Lord Zaros was forced to intervene personally. He *quarantined* this whole district - simply buried it beneath the earth.
I thought the remains of Croesus were destroyed. They assured me they were destroyed!
They say that of all the Elder Gods, Bik holds intelligent life in the greatest contempt.
She must have found Croesus beneath the graveyard and revived it. Even now it feeds on the ancient dead.
It's already massacred every defender on this front. If we don't drive it back, it will tear the cathedral to pieces.

Kerapac's life was spent fighting to free his people from the elder gods' chains.
But in his hubris, he succeeded only in chaining himself and the unwitting Nodon.

From below, a great shudder rose. The walls of the chamber began to buckle and crumble.
A mountain fell on Kerapac's device, annihilating it.
Kerapac and the World Guardian fled the ruins to avoid the same fate.
The island of Anachronia was calm and still, blissfully unaware of the rising menace.

Then, a gentle rumbling. Slowly it grew and grew until it felt
as if the ground beneath their feet would tear itself apart.
The elder god Ful cleaved through the earth, and in her rage tore the volcano asunder.
The elder gods were awake, and they were not pleased.

The dragonkin of the Dactyl were well regarded for their scientific prowess,
and none were as renowned as Kerapac.

It was to riotous applause that Kerapac unveiled his latest invention.
A device he promised would spark a new dawn of dragonkin science.
A machine capable of generating limitless power by flooding the world with corruption.

The possibilities were endless.
He believed that with power of this scale, the dragonkin would
rival the creators themselves.

Before Kerapac could celebrate his creation,
the Elder Gods' displeasure was made known.
Jas, the eldest of them, laid waste to the dragonkin cities.

In moments, the work of centuries was undone
and the dragonkin fled in terror.

Jas bound the dragonkin to the Catalyst,
an elder artefact of great power.

The dragonkin sought the power of the Elder Gods,
and their wish was granted.

Orthen was the first city built by the dragonkin upon their arrival on Gielinor, razed by the elder gods...
Your research team has discovered lots of materials from Orthen.
An authority on dragons and the dragonkin, and expert natural historian.

The team are not yet sure what factor determines if a dragonkin is interred in a coffin or cremated with their ashes stored in urns. Those interred, however, have these orgone-decorated stone masks placed over their faces.

This piece of scientific equipment generates a controlled flame for heating flasks. The little dragon head motif at the top makes it look like it is breathing out the fire - an interesting decorative detail not often seen with dragonkin artefacts.

Compared to scalpels used by other races, this one looks relatively grim and nasty - almost akin to an implement of torture - but given how hardy dragonkin are thought to be, it's likely necessary to pierce and cut their tough hides.

This calendar doesn't appear to correspond with any current or known calendars, which makes sense given dragonkin civilisation predates our history. Researchers are trying to interpret it, looking for any doomsday prophecies.

While not a weapon, this ceremonial staff could certainly still be used as one. It appears that, even in death, the dragonkin are prepared for a fight. They must have been through a lot as a species, and still yet survive.

'Dish' is a loose term for this contraption, which is predominantly made of gold. It is certainly not for storing fruit in, nor serving food. There appears to be a space for one of these atop the 'giant' golden pyramid in Xolo City.

We've been unable to determine the meaning of the term 'kilaya', though we know this is what they are called from journals among other grave goods. It's akin to a four-bladed spike or dagger, but appears to be ceremonial.

This smooth egg-shaped stone has a carving on it, though there is still speculation as to what it depicts. The competing theories are that it is either two dragonkin hands drawing in cosmic power or two dragonkin beneath a waterfall.

Elements of the design of this device suggest a similar function to dragonkin 'effigies', but also blends in elements of the 'pylons' occasionally discovered inside Orthen ruins. It appears that this device can be worn on the head.

The team believe the word 'meditation' to be somewhat euphemistic, going by analysis on the residues found in examples of these pipes. Indeed, one researcher's 'detailed analysis' had them seeing dancing pink dragons for a time.

This flask, made almost entirely of orthenglass save for a small amount of dragon metal around the neck, has a very distinctive shape. Within some of those discovered, we have been able to take samples of ages-old potions.

A translation for the word 'pasaha' still eludes us, but it is clear to see this is some sort of lasso. Given where it was found, this was likely used for the trapping and corralling of dinosaurs, and then also as some kind of leash.

Due to the totems some visitors to Anachronia have been discovering, it is speculated that this portable variant contained a small mote of the power that their larger cousins contain. It certainly shares some similar aesthetic designs.

These goggles are clearly designed to fit a dragonkin head (we tested their fit on Mr Mordaut, who is the closest model we have). He informed us that the orgone-tinted glass ever-so-slightly corrected his long-sightedness.

We call this an idol, but given the scale of the surrounding environment, it stands more as a statue within this model city. It seems to depict a particular nasty rex dinosaur. The team hope the real one was just as small.

Given the dragonkin propensity for long bouts of hibernation, it is theorised that interred kin were left with these bells, in case they were wrongfully presumed deceased. Waking up from a nap inside of a tomb would be quite traumatic.

These bowls typically contain a 'striker', which would have been run around the rim of the bowl to create a pleasing vibration - this being the 'singing' aspect. It would predominantly have been used in meditative practices.

We are unsure what the purpose of these vazara artefacts is beyond ceremonial. It presents as a club-like weapon, and has detailing that suggests it being both indestructible and unstoppable, but what if two vazara were to clash...?

This tiny (presumably) mining helmet has odd design elements, such as a vertical fluting at the rear and what seem to be eye holes towards the front. It appears to be made from reclaimed dragon metal, decorated with gold.

The team can only but presume these small tools were used as pickaxes by very small creatures. While there is only the one gold rock found in Xolo City, it would have been a relative motherlode to such a tiny people.

This shield has a striking motif on its front, which looks to be a stylised salamander head with its tongue out (or perhaps spitting fire?). From the back, it seems to be at least partially constructed from a set of protective goggles.

As with other Xolo artefacts, this spear also seems to have elements reclaimed from dragonkin objects. In this case, the base is a dragon scalpel, but it has been reshaped and then decorated with a gaudy amount of gold.

Orthen, though evidently not the only dragonkin settlement
to be found on Gielinor, was both its first and its greatest.

When Anachronia was brought forward in time, it gave us
the rare opportunity to study dragonkin civilisation,
even if only via the ruins of Orthen.

What secrets might we uncover about the dragonkin race from pre-history?
And what was their life like before the elder god curse that befell them?

Rumours abound among archaeologists of buried hoards of treasure, nefarious
entities waiting to be freed into the world, technologies beyond our own...

By all accounts, the dragonkin endured many hardships to even
arrive on this world. Their survival a constant struggle;
every scrap of progress a hard-won battle.

Yet at their height, they were a technologically and socially advanced
people who had not lost sight of their cultural and spiritual roots.

We see them only as a threat, but their story is one of tragedy.
Perhaps there is hope they may one day reclaim some of their lost grandeur.

Regardless, the legacy of their original civilisation lives on
in the form of dragons, the newly returned dinosaurs,
and the mysterious (and elusive) Xolo tribe.

We've stumbled upon many vats filled with dragonkin in suspended hibernation.
On careful closer inspection, the team has determined that a number of tubes have malfunctioned, killing the dragonkin that were within them.
Within the dragonkin crypt lies a sizeable funeral pyre.

It appears that only dragonkin of a certain level of reverence were interred in ossuaries. Most kin that died appear to have been cremated instead, their remains left in urns stored in reliquaries also found within these crypts.
The autopsy table found within the observation outpost is quite ominous.

Further investigation suggests that the dragonkin were actually very conscientious and ethical before they were cursed. The outpost was a place of learning, not cruelty (though some on the team feel these two things are synonymous).
A strange device sits at the heart of the Moksha ritual site - its purpose unknown.

Study suggests this device could separate a person's mind from their body...assuming it ever worked. Archaeologists have been advised to take great care around this device (though in some cases, it might be an improvement).
Rumours of a hidden city of gold were not so unfounded, it seems.

The model city built of gold within the ruins of Orthen is as mysterious as mysteries come. Archaeologists have been reporting tools going missing and think they keep hearing hushed whispering, but none of this is yet substantiated.
It seems as though the dragonkin portal device is part of an entire teleportation network. Research should determine how to power up the connections to other locations.

The teleportation device is clearly a combination of ritual magic and technology. It appears as though it is running extremely low on whatever magical energy is powering it. The team suggest adding some ancient vis to the destination device located at the observation outpost in the north east - it could work as a substitute magical resource.
Adding ancient vis activated an additional node on the teleportation network. Others however, remain inactive.

One of the interns has a theory that the energy in the remaining teleportation devices is not refracting through the circuits correctly. The team feel that this theory may be worth exploring. It was suggested that loading up on orthenglass and attempting to correctly refract the energy circuit in a destination device may enable that destination on the network once more. The next logical device is located at the Moksha ritual site.
Adding orthenglass activated an additional node on the teleportation network. The last destination however, remains inactive.

After a long period of investigating, the team could not figure out what was wrong with the last remaining portal device. As a last-ditch suggestion, one young archaeologist suggested boosting the device with quintessence. They shrugged at you, and exclaimed that it worked at Stormguard.

I was not always Azzanadra, your trusted friend.
Six thousand years ago I was Azzanadra, Pontifex Maximus of the Zarosian Empire.
I maintained civilisation and the rule of my lord against all those who called themselves gods.
I am very familiar with Seren's influence.
We can no longer rely on this council.
They are completely under her sway now.
In time they will recover their initiative, but for now they are nothing but puppets.
Seren is obsessed with the adult elder gods.
Her guilt and shame blind her to the true threat.
It is not the adults who are destined to destroy us. It is their unborn children.
If they wake, they will devour this world, and in time, all worlds.

If the best these fools can do is waste their time on senseless
appeasement, then it falls to us to save them.
We must find the elder god eggs.
This world was lush, once. Green and flourishing. A perfect womb for the sleeping gods.
Within their shells, they slumbered in a yolk of incredible power.

The currents of magic drove more and more energy into the eggs,
until they reached bursting point.
Sensing the impending birth of their young, the adults pressed in close.
With a touch they imparted their identities and their memories.
The eggs burst open, and the hatchlings within emerged, ravenous.
Their mere presence drained all life from the cavern around them.
Within moments every other living thing nearby was dead, drained of all life.
Nothing could stop them. The world was doomed.
Further and further their reach expanded, blanketing everything.
Further and further their reach expanded, blanketing everything.
Minutes later, Freneskae was a desolate husk.
The sated hatchlings travelled out into the universe to remake it.

At the time, none of us realised the significance of the events that were about to unfold.
The followers of Zaros came first, descending on the Monolith to seize it for the dark lord.

My fellow ancients, awoken from their tombs,
commanded traitor knights to begin their assault.
But the worst was still to come.
At last his plans had come to fruition.

With implacable will he forced it open, revealing the truth
that lay at its heart - a tear in the fabric of our reality.
Then he departed from this world, heedless of the devastation that would follow in his wake.
From that same gateway came beings of pure shadow, and with them a torrent of dark energy.
Left unchecked, it would choke our world.
But the worst was still to come.
The invaders from beyond proved too much for the brave allies.
Yet hope was not lost - Gielinor had defenders still.

The TokHaar, the hands who created this world, the servants of
the Elder Gods themselves, stood with us.
But the worst was still to come.

The priest, my friend, his heart filled with shame and confusion,
stood before the doom his efforts had wrought.
He grappled with the gateway, forcing it closed as it sought to consume him.
The Monolith snapped shut, but the backlash had nowhere else to go.
Pain cut through him as the corrupting energies tore into his body.
Silence enveloped him...but there would be no peace for the most faithful.
The desolate scream of the new god filled the air.

In the aftermath of the devastation, the TokHaar looked at what the
witless surface dwellers had done to their world.
Everything would have to be dismantled, starting with their former allies.
But the worst was still to come.

The invaders may have been defeated but the foul power
that seeped from the gateway has already done its work.
The Elder God eggs, imperiled by the poison, are hatching.
The young within will feast on our world.
Now the worst is upon us.

Leng was one of the first planets created by the Elder Gods.
It was no paradise, but it birthed an industrious civilisation whose name is now long forgotten.
When the icy comets appeared in the sky, the people of Leng had no idea what awaited them.
The crashing comets wrought devastation as they landed, but something worse rose out of the craters..
The incorporeal invaders formed towering suits of armour from the ice they brought with them.
That same ice spread across the whole world, covering the cities and freezing their people.
Their work done, the glacors stood vigil over a silent, dead world for countless aeons.
When the Elder God Wen needed powerful servants, she found them waiting in this inhospitable place.
Anathema suffused the planet and its denizens. Could she really unleash them against Gielinor - the hatchery for her precious egg?
Unwilling to approach such tainted beings, she opened portals for them, and turned her face from the destruction to come.
My people, cursed, bound, in pain. United in our suffering.
I could not imagine a worse fate.
Bound once more to Her service, now I suffer alone.
I am commanded to secure the eggs.
For this I require an army.
Rather than lift a finger they slept through the curse.
The Needle. The Conduit. The very tools of my oppressor.
The source of my power. The walls of my prison.
As long as I wield them I can never be free, but she will not let me give them up.
Jas seeks only to preserve what is left of her kind. For that she would trade the universe.
Once I would have made the same trade.
The only thing that matters to me now is my freedom. Let everything else wither.

I'm interested in anything found in Senntisten.
An ancient city buried beneath the Varrock Dig Site.
Reduces cooldown of Surge, Escape, Bladed Dive and Barge by 50%.
Senntisten was the capital city of the Zarosian Empire during the Second and Third Age...
Your research team has discovered lots of materials from Senntisten.
The apex cap was worn by the Zarosian priesthood in Senntisten. The strange shape of the cap represents the tendrils that Zaros used to defeat the hydra deity Loarnab.

Magicians in the empire would create curse tablets. Sheets of metal on which the name of an enemy would be inscribed. The tablet was then buried in a graveyard so that dark spirits would know the name of the target.
Citizens would use intricate and beautifully decorated amphoras to display their wealth and status. Many would display religious lessons or parables as a further sign of the citizen's devotion.
These urns were used by the ancient priests of Senntisten in funeral rites. Miasma would be used to symbolically guide the spirit to Erebus as the miasma would create a trail the spirit could follow.

The blood of the dead was collected in these funerary urns as a reminder of the life lost. The urns would then be magically infused so that the blood could remain as a constant source of ancient magick creating a lasting legacy for the deceased.

The urn of ice would be used in ancient Senntisten funerals to chill and thus preserve the body of the deceased. The body would be frozen by the magic and the urn would keep it cold and holding back the ravages of decay.
Shadow urns were used in Senntisten funerals to obscure the deceased's soul from dark spirits on the journey to Erebus.

Urns empowered with the ancient magick of smoke would be used as a marker for the deceased. Placed at their grave for days after their passing, anyone would be able to look in the air and see a trail of smoke indicating a life lost.

The colosseum was a great spectacle in the empire and one of the most popular forms of entertainment. Gladiators could find themselves elevated from criminals to beloved heroes. Few survived to enjoy the adulation for long.

Gladiators would be armed with two weapons, a sword and a net. Over time a gladiator would favour a particular sword and many would give their swords names to terrify their opponents and impress the crowds.
A strange sculpture representing the ancient elements. The hand of ancients was placed in the homes of citizens to ward off bad spirits that might try and sneak inside to cause mischief.
These robes were worn by the members of the church as a sign of their religious purity. They would be immaculately maintained and washed in a mixture of perfumes giving them a distinct aroma.

Due to their secretive nature it was necessary for the members of the Inquisition to have an official badge of office in cases of mistaken identity. These badges were subtly enchanted so that they would be impossible to forge.

This armour would be used for secret ceremonies among the Inquisition or when members would need to gather, such as in the Inquisition office. They incorporated slightly strange proportions to try and disguise the species of the wearer so that as much anonymity as possible could be maintained.
The sinister mask of the Inquisitor was designed purely to hide their features. The mouth was sealed shut to imply the silent power of the Inquisition as well as their oath to secrecy.

This rod was worn by physicians around the empire as a symbol of their craft. Not only did it demonstrate their healing skills, by referencing Loarnab's unnatural powers of regeneration, but also served as a reminder that anything can be overcome.

The demon drawn chariot races of Senntisten were a marvel to behold. Mighty demons would drag a human or vampyre chariot rider across the skies of the city in magnificent races against other teams. It was one of the most popular forms of entertainment in the city.
This image depicts the fall of Loarnab, one of the most popular religious stories in the empire. It clearly shows Zaros's triumph over the hydra god.
There is a hidden part of the Cathedral connected to the statues and the Shadow Realm. If we can uncover the secret, imagine what we could discover.
We uncovered what appears to be a secret laboratory dedicated to studying the Monolith. What was Zaros doing here?
The markets of Senntisten are a mystery to us. Was their trade system as carefully organised as their political structure?
The markets of Senntisten were carefully licensed, with various tiers of status that granted access to more lucrative contracts and desirable tax breaks.
North of the plaza lies the crumbling ruins of a magnificent bridge. With some work, we could make it more accessible.
With some carefully placed scaffolding, we can now access the magnificent view of the bridge over the Senntisten waterways.
The Colosseum was once the central entertainment hub of the Empire. What games did they play here?
The Colosseum was home to brutal gladiatorial battles and magnificent demon-drawn chariot races. It would have been a crowded building in its heyday.

I have been a chieftain, a gladiator, a warlord, a demigod.
I was born into a world where all were free. Then, the Empire came.
Conquered my people. Threw me into the pits. I was to die there.
Nothing could challenge me. Demons, dragons and vampyres fell to my blade.
From the great Tribune Torva, I won back my freedom.
I went in search of worthier foes.
Beneath a distant volcano, I found the ultimate arena.
The TokHaar - who shaped the mountains at the dawn of time - battled endlessly.
They called me TzKal - Champion of the Fire. The first outsider to defeat them all.
For my prize, I claimed the Elder Kiln itself.
For centuries it changed me. I became undying.
Like TokHaar, I am born again within the Kiln. Unlike TokHaar, my mind is my own.
The God Wars called to me. The TokHaar would not follow, but the lava beasts would.
We carved through the weak surface dwellers effortlessly. It was only Bandos himself who stopped me.
Coward. He chained me within the Kiln.
When Ful needed an army, she had no use for the failed TokHaar.
They were remade. Artisans reforged into soldiers.
Now they are the TzekHaar, united in purpose.
They serve without question. Mine to command.
Ful wants the eggs, but I pay no heed to her desires.
I seek only the glory of combat. Is anyone in this alliance worthy?
Refuse me, and your world will end.
